route: private chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex (chatgpt auth mode); no proxy, so the request bodies were not captured

method.turn1: codex exec --json -m gpt-6.1-sol -s read-only --skip-git-repo-check -c model_reasoning_effort='low' -c model_reasoning_summary='none' '<prompt>'
method.turn2: codex exec resume <thread_id> --json --skip-git-repo-check -c model_reasoning_effort='low' -c model_reasoning_summary='none' 'Turn 2. Reply with the single word OK.'
method.numbers: JSONL event token_count.info.last_token_usage (per turn). turn.completed.usage is the session total, so it must not be used per turn.
method.promptShape: 'Reference material, ignore its content.' + N words of generated padding + 'Turn 1. Reply with the single word OK.'; no tools were invoked, matching the shape of scripts/cache-parity/provider-probe.mjs.

reading: Codex CLI reuses only a 12288-token block of its own fixed harness once the first prompt carries any user content: turn 2 reads 12288 of the prior 18552 or 24840 tokens. With no user padding at all it reused 17664 of the prior 17887.

That collapse reproduces at two pad sizes (665 and 12552 tokens), so it is a property of the CLI on this route, not a one-off. It is not explained by the bodies: chatgpt-mode traffic was not proxied, so whether the harness tail or the user message differs byte-wise between turns is unverified.

Prism, on the same model and account, reuses 8192 of its 8334-token prefix across turns regardless of the new turn's size (9809 cached of all input) and grows input by 18 tokens per turn where codex grows by 708-3085.

Fairness note: codex's 12288 is a permanent server-side harness cache shared across runs, so its very first request already starts 69% offset while Prism's first request starts at 0. This is a per-turn steady-state comparison on the same conversation shape, not a cold-start one.
